Comment incorrectly states that Django QuerySets handle negative slicing - they actually raise an `AssertionError`. This misleading documentation could cause confusion and bugs.

Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing - when enable_advanced_features is true and cursor.offset is negative, line 882 passes the negative offset directly to queryset[start_offset:stop], which raises AssertionError. Any superuser hitting the audit logs endpoint with optimized_pagination=true and a crafted cursor containing a negative offset will get a 500 error. The fix should clamp start_offset to 0 or reject negative offsets with a BadPaginationError.
BasePaginator.get_result change uses start_offset = max(0, offset) for next cursor but still uses raw offset in duplicate-trim check (len(results) == offset + limit + extra), causing divergence
organization_context.member.has_global_access is accessed without null check - superusers without org membership will have member=None causing AttributeError
Django QuerySet does not support negative slicing - the negative offset feature will crash at runtime when enable_advanced_features=True and cursor.offset < 0

OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/math.ceil on datetime objects instead of epoch-ms conversion like DateTimePaginator, causing TypeError and 500 errors on every non-empty page with optimized_pagination=true

OptimizedCursorPaginator.value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor value (an integer timestamp) instead of converting it back to a datetime, so build_queryset will compare an integer against a DateTimeField on page 2+, causing type mismatch errors. It should convert back using datetime.fromtimestamp() like DateTimePaginator does.

Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing. When `enable_advanced_features` is True and `cursor.offset < 0`, this code will raise an `AssertionError` at runtime with message 'Negative indexing is not supported.'

get_item_key assumes a numeric key, but the paginator is used with order_by=-datetime in the audit logs endpoint; calling math.floor/ceil on a datetime will raise a TypeError.

OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor()/math.ceil() directly on datetime objects (line 839), which raises TypeError since datetime does not implement __floor__. The method should convert datetime to float timestamp first like DateTimePaginator does.

New optimized_pagination query parameter is undocumented in API docs or changelog

Admin-only gate is ineffective: has_global_access defaults to True for members, and request.user.is_superuser reads raw DB flag instead of is_active_superuser(request), bypassing superuser-session check

`OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` applies `math.floor`/`math.ceil` directly to the raw attribute value. When paginating by `-datetime`, the value is a `datetime` object, and `math.floor(datetime)` raises `TypeError`. The `DateTimePaginator` it replaces handles this correctly by first converting to a float timestamp.
RpcUserOrganizationContext.member is documented as optional, so organization_context.member.has_global_access can raise if member is None, causing a 500 error
Potential AttributeError when organization_context.member is None, causing organization_context.member.has_global_access to raise AttributeError

Misleading comments in Cursor class describe performance optimization for negative offsets but the Cursor class itself doesn't implement any special handling - actual implementation is in OptimizedCursorPaginator

OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/math.ceil on a datetime object instead of converting to epoch ms like DateTimePaginator does, causing TypeError (HTTP 500) on every request with optimized_pagination=true that returns rows

issues.claim: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/math.ceil directly on the sort key. With order_by='-datetime' in the audit logs endpoint, that key is a datetime, so a TypeError is raised. DateTimePaginator avoids this by converting to an epoch timestamp first.

OptimizedCursorPaginator.value_from_cursor returns the raw integer cursor.value without converting it back to a datetime as DateTimePaginator does. build_queryset therefore compares a datetime field against an integer on subsequent pages.

The enable_advanced check in the audit logs endpoint accesses organization_context.member.has_global_access without a None check. member is None for callers without membership, such as superusers, API keys/org auth tokens, legacy org ApiKeys and internal-integration proxy users, so an AttributeError is raised.

When enable_advanced_features is true, OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result passes a user-supplied negative cursor.offset directly into queryset[start_offset:stop]. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing, so a crafted cursor (e.g. 0:-10:0) raises an error that is not converted to BadPaginationError and results in a 500.

Comments and docstrings in the patch contain false or marketing-style claims. Examples are that the Django ORM properly handles negative slicing, 'sophisticated pagination patterns', and 'safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level'.

The change to the shared BasePaginator.get_result clamps negative next-cursor offsets to 0 with max(0, offset). Negative prev-cursor offsets still reach the queryset slice and raise errors, which contradicts the comment saying negative offsets are allowed.
BasePaginator.get_result uses start_offset = max(0, offset) for slicing but still uses the raw offset in the duplicate-trim check (len(results) == offset + limit + extra), so the two diverge.
The comments added to the Cursor class in cursors.py say negative offsets are now allowed or optimized. No code in Cursor changed, and int(offset) already accepted negative values.

OptimizedCursorPaginator is a near line-for-line copy of BasePaginator.get_result and Paginator's key/cursor methods, plus broken additions. It builds the same queryset, makes the same count call and uses the same slice, so it does not deliver the claimed performance improvement.
No tests cover OptimizedCursorPaginator, the optimized_pagination=true endpoint branch and its cursor handling, or the change to BasePaginator.get_result.
The patch adds trailing whitespace and extra blank lines at end of file, which fail the repo's trailing-whitespace and end-of-file-fixer pre-commit hooks.
The endpoint's if/else block repeats the same self.paginate(...) call, differing only in paginator_cls and one kwarg.
The enable_advanced_features constructor flag has a single caller that always passes True. Its name does not indicate that it enables negative-offset slicing.
The code imports OptimizedCursorPaginator, which does not exist.

The admin gate checks the raw request.user.is_superuser DB flag instead of is_active_superuser(request), which bypasses the active superuser-session check. has_global_access also defaults to True for members, so the gate does not restrict access to admins.
The new optimized_pagination query parameter is not documented in the API docs or changelog.
